notes: Patch format. Only the listed fields change; every other field on the record is preserved.
No option label or option weight changes anywhere. Do not touch options[] or scoring{}.

normalise_options on burnout adds value to each option object. It does NOT change any label text and does NOT touch scoring{}. This is the one exception to the 'no option changes' rule and it is shape-only.
All interpretation strings are now populated. Zero placeholders remain in the payload.

question_options relabels depression-q10 and anxiety-q8 in place. Question ids are NOT changed and the 4-point 0-3 scale shape is NOT changed - only the four label strings and the scoring map keys. This is permitted because both items are is_scored:false and belong to no score.
meta.interpretation_copy: All 7 __NEEDS_COPY__ strings drafted by Claude on 2026-09-08 at Vedanshu's instruction. Kartik has not signed off on them.

question_text.depression-q3: Trouble falling or staying asleep or sleeping too much
question_text.depression-q6: Feeling bad about yourself-or that you’re a failure or have let yourself or your family down
question_text.depression-q7: Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
question_text.depression-q8: Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed. Or, the opposite - being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
question_text.depression-q9: Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way

depression-q10.reason: The item asks 'How difficult have the above problems made it...' but offers the frequency scale, so the only possible answers are 'Not at all / Several days / More than half the days / Nearly every day'. Live today; required:true, so every respondent is forced through it.
depression-q10.scale_shape_unchanged: 4 options, weights 0-3, same order, same numeric prefixes
depression-q10.safe_because: this question is is_scored:false and appears in no score's items[], so no value is ever derived from it. Relabelling cannot move any score, past or future.
depression-q10.known_effect: stored responses for this question still hold the old frequency string. Nothing scores them, so no number changes; a raw-answer view would show a string that no longer matches an option.

anxiety-q8.reason: The item asks 'How difficult have the above problems made it...' but offers the frequency scale, so the only possible answers are 'Not at all / Several days / More than half the days / Nearly every day'. Live today; required:true, so every respondent is forced through it.

question_text.stress-q1: In the last month, how often have you been upset because of something that happened unexpectedly?
question_text.stress-q2: In the last month, how often have you felt that you were unable to control the important things in your life?
question_text.stress-q3: In the last month, how often have you felt nervous and stressed?
question_text.stress-q4: In the last month, how often have you felt confident about your ability to handle your personal problems?
question_text.stress-q5: In the last month, how often have you felt that things were going your way?
question_text.stress-q6: In the last month, how often have you found that you could not cope with all the things that you had to do?
question_text.stress-q7: In the last month, how often have you been able to control irritations in your life?

new_questions.text: In the last month, how often have you felt that you were on top of things?
In the last month, how often have you been angered because of things that happened that were outside of your control?
In the last month, how often have you felt difficulties were piling up so high that you could not overcome them?

question_text.sleep-q8: Finally how long have you had a problem with your sleep?

question_text.balance-q1: Conditions at work are unpleasant or sometimes even unsafe.
question_text.balance-q2: I feel that my job is negatively affecting my physical or emotional well-being.
question_text.balance-q3: I have too much work to do an/or too many unreasonable deadlines.
question_text.balance-q4: I find it difficult to express my opinions or feelings about my job conditions to my superiors.
question_text.balance-q5: I feel that job pressures interfere with my family or personal life.
question_text.balance-q6: I feel that I have inadequate control or input over my work duties.
question_text.balance-q7: I receive inadequate recognition or rewards for good performance.
question_text.balance-q8: I am unable to fully utilize my skills and talents at work.

question_text.burnout-q1: At work, I feel mentally exhausted
question_text.burnout-q2: Everything I do at work requires a great deal of effort
question_text.burnout-q3: After a day at work, I find it hard to recover my energy
question_text.burnout-q4: At work, I feel physically exhausted
question_text.burnout-q5: When I get up in the morning, I lack the energy to start a new day at work
question_text.burnout-q6: I want to be active at work, but somehow I am unable to manage
question_text.burnout-q7: When I exert myself at work, I quickly get tired
question_text.burnout-q8: At the end of my working day, I feel mentally exhausted and drained
question_text.burnout-q19: At work, I feel unable to control my emotions

normalise_options.reason: burnout is the only assessment whose options[] are bare strings; every other assessment stores [{text,value}]. deriveScale() therefore falls back to the per-question scoring map for this one instrument only.
normalise_options.operation: replace each question's options[] with the object form below. Label text is byte-identical to the existing string, so no stored response is orphaned. Values are copied from that question's own scoring map (all 23 maps are identical - verified).
normalise_options.postcondition: after this, option.value is populated on all 7 assessments, so a validation guard may be written against option.value uniformly and deriveScale()'s array-index fallback becomes unreachable.

set.description: Nine items scored 0-3, range 0-27, band edges 5/10/15/20. Item 9 now carries the published PHQ-9 wording (revision 2026-09-08); the previous softened local wording is retired.

bands.label: Major depressive disorder is likely
bands.interpretation: This brief screen suggests it is worth looking at depression as well.

bands.interpretation: Mild anxiety symptoms.

set.name: Stress (10 items, 0-4)
set.description: Perceived Stress Scale, ten items each scored 0-4, four reversed (q4, q5, q7, q8). Higher total means more stress. Achievable range 0-40.

bands.label: Low Stress
bands.interpretation: You are managing stress well.

bands.label: Moderate Stress
bands.interpretation: Stress is starting to affect your life.

bands.label: High Stress
bands.interpretation: High stress levels. We recommend giving this attention.

bands.label: Healthy Sleep
bands.interpretation: Your sleep patterns look healthy overall.

bands.label: Poor Sleep
bands.interpretation: Your sleep is disturbed often enough to be affecting your days.

bands.label: Very Poor Sleep
bands.interpretation: Your sleep is substantially disrupted. Structured support is recommended.

set.description: Eight workplace-strain items each scored 1-5, none reversed (all items are negatively worded from the 2026-09-08 revision). Higher total means more strain. Achievable range 8-40.

bands.label: Nil

bands.label: Fairly Low
bands.interpretation: There is some strain at work, but it is within a range most people manage.

bands.label: Moderate
bands.interpretation: Work is putting real strain on you. Worth addressing before it builds further.

bands.label: Severe
bands.interpretation: Your work conditions are placing heavy strain on you. We recommend giving this attention.

bands.label: Potentially Dangerous
bands.interpretation: Your work conditions are placing serious strain on your wellbeing. We recommend speaking with a professional.

bands.label: Low
bands.interpretation: Low burnout risk.

bands.label: Normal
bands.interpretation: Within the normal range, with some signs worth watching.

bands.label: High
bands.interpretation: High burnout risk.

bands.label: Poor
bands.interpretation: Your wellbeing has been low. We recommend giving this attention.

bands.label: Good
bands.interpretation: Good wellbeing.
